top_choice_rationale: P001 (Autor, Dorn, Hanson) credits a first-order empirical contribution: transparent local-labour-market designs showing that exposure to import competition produced concentrated, persistent adjustment costs. The designs were contested on shift-share identification, exposure measures and persistence for about a decade, and the sign and local concentration of the central finding survived in qualified form while magnitudes were refined. The core papers are mature, and attribution is the tightest on the slate because the programme is jointly authored by the three. A narrow citation on exposure, employment, wages and adjustment, with no claim about effect size or the origins of the task framework, limits the cost of leaving out Katz and the task lineage. P002 (Helpman, Melitz) ranks second: it is mature and has a clean two-person core, but its priority questions (Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum), the 2008 overlap and structure-dependent welfare claims remain unresolved from the supplied evidence. P000 is ranked last because at least two proposals credit substantive, mature achievements.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my field of labour economics is adjacent to P001 and I presented the 2023 prize, but I have no listed co-authorship or institutional tie to Autor, Dorn, Hanson, Helpman or Melitz
